findings.title: Recycle acknowledged browser receipt markers without reviving stale operations
findings.trigger: Ordinary completed mutations accumulate one permanent harness.acknowledged.v1.<UUID>=1 localStorage key apiece (most non-input writes acknowledge automatically). The 200-record guard excludes these keys. Continued use of the same origin eventually fills its localStorage quota, even when previous operations were all handled; any existing origin data reduces headroom.
findings.observed: Actual current-source reproduction with a 65536-byte synthetic quota completed 531 accepted/acknowledged operations, retaining 531 markers (64782 bytes). Operation 532 became accepted but acknowledgement failed with QuotaExceededError. Re-query/reconcile of that original accepted receipt succeeded; acknowledgement and creation of an unrelated operation still failed with QuotaExceededError. The UI catches and displays the storage exception; no silent dispatch or automatic replay was observed.
findings.scale: Each generated UUID marker uses 122 UTF-16 bytes in the fixture accounting. A hypothetical 5 MiB allowance corresponds to roughly 42974 markers before overhead or other entries; this is an order-of-magnitude estimate, not a measured browser quota or a claim of near-term failure.
findings.impact: Persistent loss of new mutation capability for a long-lived browser origin, with no product-supported local marker compaction/recovery. Handling the remaining accepted record cannot release capacity because acknowledgement must first add another key. Server receipt generation maintenance does not remove browser markers. Clearing origin data manually can discard unrelated pending/unknown recovery identities and is not an adequate safe recovery flow.
findings.requirements: OP-05 requires visible fail-closed storage errors and includes reaching capacity, handling a record and retrying. The current path satisfies visible fail-closed behavior but has no capacity recovery for handled markers. OP-04 also requires late observations never undo an acknowledged fact; existing markers fulfill that invariant and must not simply be deleted.
findings.recommendation: Provide a bounded local retention/maintenance design with a persistent generation floor or equivalent cross-tab coordination that safely retires handled markers. Preserve pending/unknown identities and suppress late writes from old tabs across compaction/reload. Offer observable local capacity status and a safe maintenance path; do not use naked TTL/removal of acknowledged keys.
findings.counterEvidence: A deliberate stale unknown write after acceptance+ack leaves a primary key present but invisible; visibleOperations and visibleAfterLateRecovery remain zero. Thus marker growth is intentional protection, and the finding concerns missing sustainable capacity recovery rather than unsafe current retry behavior.

limitations: No full-suite run, real supplier/model/MCP invocation, public HTTPS deployment or integration account validation was performed.

No rendered browser viewport, real OS IME, mobile device, screen reader, real browser quota or live microphone/terminal integration verification. Those remain integration limitations, not inferred successes.

web/VERIFICATION.md was structurally inspected only; its historical result prose was deliberately excluded as evidence. CSS received complete parser/selector inspection rather than pixel-based visual testing.

Parent reassigned all 69 web tests to other reviewers; only three fully read tests are extra coverage here. web/tests/prompts.test.tsx lines 1-140 were an incidental partial read and are not included in inspectedFiles.

methodDetails.basis: Independent current-source audit. Read repository AGENTS.md first. No old implementation, Git history or historical audit reports used as behavioral evidence. Current README and OP-04/OP-05 acceptance clauses consulted for storage invariants.
methodDetails.code: Read every assigned TS/TSX/HTML/JSON implementation/configuration file in full (large files in sequential chunks; truncated ranges reread). Followed UI entry points, shared hooks and helpers, user authorizations, API mutation receipt ownership, session/connection/project/thread identities, aborts and late responses, failed/unknown/reconnect paths, draft revisions, media/input validation, resource budgets and dangerous-action confirmations.

structural.method: Parsed complete CSS text with the installed Vite dependency PostCSS; traversed all rules/declarations/imports/URLs and visibility selectors, checked responsive rules with direct reading. All seven parsed; no imports or url() fetches; hidden selectors preserve display:none. No rendered viewport/OS accessibility claim.
Full bytes scanned for Markdown structure, fences and local links only. Historical result prose is deliberately not used as audit evidence.
